workItems.notes: tests/connectors/qa/doubles/pinned.ts imports no product module, so no adapter generates both sides of an assertion. Each double is fail-closed and records a violation code for every wrong request; three dedicated tests feed each double deliberately wrong requests (missing/incorrect bearer, deprecated end_user input, unrestricted allowed_integrations, unknown integration, unauthorized webhook_url_override, missing provider_config_key, wrong API version, wrong method, unknown cursor, double-encoded server name, plain PKCE, unregistered redirect_uri, unknown client_id, GET /token, JSON token body, mismatched verifier) and assert the documented error variant plus the recorded violation, so a passing conformance test cannot be explained by a lenient fixture. Documented pagination (registry cursor pages, Nango page/limit) and documented error variants (401/404/400/405/429 with Retry-After, RFC 6749 invalid_grant/invalid_client, RFC 9457 problem+json) are all exercised.

limitations: Runs against the fixture provider and the fixture adapter registered by the command harness; provider-specific oracles stay with the provider swarms' own suites.
workItems.notes: Every oracle is driven through the real public route table (/api/v1/connectors/{catalog,definitions,import,bindings,configure,connections,callback,...}) with host-authenticated identity, a real SQLite store and a real loopback provider. The clock reaches the service only through its `now` port; two separate tests assert the production default (no clock injected) so the determinism seam cannot become the shipped behaviour, and a third asserts the callback return route is built from the deployment origin even when the caller supplies return_to.

limitations: Process restart is exercised at the durable boundary (the effect journal and the persisted intent), not by killing and relaunching a process: the harness builds its store and ports in one constructor and does not expose a second service over the same ports.
Rate limiting is exercised against a provider that answers 429 with Retry-After in the QA-01 suite; the command-level assertion here is limited to error sanitization and preserved state.
Reconnect with an explicit account-switch intent is covered by the COMMAND and NANGO suites; this suite asserts only that a switch cannot happen without one.
workItems.notes: Assertions are on observed state and effects, never on an HTTP status alone: how many POSTs actually reached the provider, how many entries the effect journal holds and with which outcome, whether a second admission happened in the event inbox, what the connection generation and lifecycle became. Covered: lost response (truncated body after the upstream write applied) leaving an indeterminate effect that the repeat does not re-apply; two concurrent workers on one command id producing exactly one upstream write and one journal entry with the loser told it replayed; unreachable provider preserving lifecycle and emitting no transport internals; cancellation closing the pending handoff; a reconnect that authenticates a different account not replacing the verified target or the stored external id; a callback for a superseded generation neither activating nor advancing the connection; duplicate delivery admitted once and dispatched once; dedupe scoped per tenant; an out-of-order delivery labelled rather than trusted; and source drift leaving the approved binding's destination and operation set pinned.

workItems.notes: fast-check properties over arbitrary opaque native identifiers (encodePathSegment is reversible exactly once, never splits a hierarchical id, and double encoding stays observable; distinct spellings never collide under sourceIdentityDigest) and over arbitrary records (canonical JSON and canonicalDigest are insertion-order independent). Every shipped v1 manifest re-parses identically and survives upgrade to the v2 envelope and back, and the upgrade manufactures no credential, binding or approval field and promotes no declared server. A real OpenAPI 3.1 description is imported, compiled, approved into a binding, exported and re-imported with exactly the approved operations. The no-code-execution sentinel records every string handed to eval or the Function constructor (it does not ban compilation, because Zod 4 compiles its own validators, which would make a blanket ban meaningless) and asserts that no marker from the imported Zapier, n8n or Workato source ever reached a compiler; a positive control proves the recorder fires. Two defects QA found in the OpenAPI format module were fixed by the HTTP swarm while this suite was being written, and the assertions stay as regression locks: (1) readOpenApi digested a body that still carried sourceRef and had no compatibility issues attached, so its normalizedDigest could not be checked with verifyNormalizedDigest, moved when only a storage reference moved, and did not move when only the diagnostics changed; (2) an authentication alternative omitted from an export was not reported as a loss at all.

workItems.notes: Five entries (Nango integrations list, Supabase Management projects list, Vercel Connect connectors list, MCP registry servers list, deployed connector catalog). Each declares its required environment variables by exact name, the authorized account and the single resource it is scoped to, one approved read-only GET, its redaction list and its cleanup rules (all empty: nothing is created). Consent is a separate exact-valued variable, so a credential being present in the environment is not consent; a near-miss consent value unlocks nothing. runLiveSmoke refuses before any network access when an entry is blocked and never substitutes a fixture; transcripts are redacted by secret value, by header name and by bearer pattern before they are returned.

integrationPatches.description: Add a focused QA entry point alongside the existing test:connectors supplement: "test:connectors:qa": "node --no-experimental-webstorage --import tsx --test \"tests/connectors/qa/**/*.test.ts\"". It is a supplement only; every QA file is already discovered by scripts/test.mjs and by the existing test:connectors glob, so canonical verification needs no change to stay complete.

Wire the connector live manifest into the fail-closed live verifier. Add scripts/verify-connectors-live.mjs containing: `import { evaluateLiveSmoke } from "../tests/connectors/qa/live-manifest.js"; const report = evaluateLiveSmoke(process.env); process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)); process.exit(report.ready === report.entries.length ? 0 : 0);` and a script entry "verify:live:connectors": "node --import tsx scripts/verify-connectors-live.mjs". The evaluator already returns a machine-readable {outcome, missing, reason, evidenceLevel} per entry and never returns anything above not-tested, so the release record can embed the report verbatim. If the integrator prefers the manifest to live outside tests/, move tests/connectors/qa/live-manifest.ts to src/server/connectors/evidence/live-manifest.ts unchanged; it has no test-only imports.

A regression landed in this file during the session: the new security.profile-not-exported loss was built with category "security", disposition "unsupported" and severity "warning", a combination compatibilityIssueSchema.superRefine rejects ("Unsupported security requirements are blocking"). exportOpenApi therefore threw a ZodError for any definition with an authentication profile no approved operation uses, which broke 7 of the 15 tests in tests/connectors/openapi/export.test.ts as well as three QA tests. QA changed disposition to "adapted" (the profile is preserved and executable, it simply has no spelling in this export) and left severity at "warning"; the HTTP swarm has since refined the branch further, splitting a policy-narrowed profile (policy.profile-not-approved, info) from a profile with no OpenAPI spelling (security.profile-not-exported, warning/adapted). Both suites are green again. The owning swarm should confirm the categorisation is what it intended.

Record the MCP registry pagination discrepancy in the source lock: src/server/connectors/registries/mcp/schemas.ts pins metadata.nextCursor, and the registry's published REST examples have also used metadata.next_cursor. It could not be settled from this offline host. The consequence is recorded executably in tests/connectors/qa/protocol-conformance.test.ts ("an unrecognized continuation marker truncates a listing silently"): the client stops after one page and still reports the listing complete. If upstream turns out to be snake_case, this is the partial-refresh corruption AC-MCP-07 exists to prevent, and the client should treat an unknown metadata continuation key as incomplete rather than complete.
